notes: Quality and execution results apply to the recorded source hashes and measured cases only.
The runtime commit is a HEAD identifier; source_files also describe uncommitted or untracked implementation at measurement time. The post-measurement review commit is not the measurement revision.
Original quality flags, execution gates, counters, fallback/error records and scope configuration remain unchanged; review does not retroactively apply newer admission gates.
Repeated kernel receipts are grouped by the entire canonical JSON receipt before redaction. All distinct receipt fields and multiplicities are retained; original dispatch ordering is discarded.

Absolute local paths and output locations are replaced with labeled relative locations. Process IDs and process identity fields are removed; foreign context entries, memory values and counts remain when recorded.
No timestamps, missing scope receipts, asset metadata hashes or end-of-run unchanged checks are reconstructed from later code.
The fixed quality budgets are retained; rejected configurations carry no validated speedup claim.

These experiments include the vendor LayerNorm correction. The recorded HEAD equals the post-review implementation commit; source hashes remain authoritative for measured code, including benchmark scripts not yet committed at measurement time.

An end-of-run source rehash is recorded as source_unchanged=true. Weight and tokenizer/config hashes describe the recorded input manifest; this native script did not record an end-of-run inputs_unchanged check, so unchanged weights or candidate-definition files across the run are not independently certified.
Requested candidate options are embedded in the record. The external candidate-definition JSON is not separately fingerprinted or rehashed at the end of the run.

Per-module attention hooks ran in untimed pilots for configured attention-policy scopes. Timed generations retained fresh request-local kernel/provider/plugin receipts without per-module hooks. Empty scope maps in cache/projection-only candidates indicate no scoped attention plugin was requested.

GPU timing qualification applies only to recorded physical-device context samples before and after individual generations. It does not certify continuous GPU exclusivity, CPU isolation or an isolated host system. The top-level pre-context discovery failed to identify the physical GPU; later case/pair samples identified it when timing was performed.

Some experiment sessions overlapped across different physical GPUs and shared the same host CPU; the two Sol sessions used their GPU sequentially. No system-isolated performance claim follows from device sampling.

Cross-KV passed bitwise latent/RGB equality, actual packed-projection execution and sampled-GPU timing admission for both seeds. Its three paired rounds per seed yielded recorded median ratios 1.0016474702449312 and 1.0010002547168766; the roughly 0.10–0.16% improvement is tiny and limited to these cases and shared-host conditions.

Recorded bootstrap confidence intervals and the selection rule are retained. Three pairs provide limited uncertainty evidence and do not establish a general speedup across workloads or independently isolated systems.

EasyCache thresholds 0.025 and 0.05 made no skips and failed the execution gate. Threshold 0.1 made skips for seed 42 but failed quality; seed 43 made no skips and failed execution. No EasyCache speedup is qualified.
